A unified theory of physics, but since that's probably not happening anytime soon I'd settle for KIC8462852 - that star system that is experiencing the bizarre light dips and fluctuations with no clear natural cause. Aside from the bizarre behavior the thing that makes that star most interesting to me is its seeming uniqueness. We've analyzed at least tens of thousands of other stars and this is the only one exhibiting this exact sort of behavior. And the current hypotheses range from planet eating (on the scale of Jupiters) to little green men. The uniqueness and lack of any sort of 'normal' explanation make this a fun little curiosity to follow.

Yeah, that's where the little green men come in with a dyson sphere type idea. One in the process of being constructed matches what's being observed near perfectly. I think further adding some credence to this idea is that it these indicators (and idea) were predicted and suggested decades prior to being observed as a potential way to locate extraterrestrial civilizations. However, the 'near perfect' part comes from from the point that one part of the prediction was that we'd see an excess of infrared energy as the product of the solar energy being reemitted from the sphere. That has not been observed. Nonetheless there are technological reasons why this might be the case if it were a sphere.

Definitely one of the most intriguing possibilities, but it's kind of the nuclear options since once you start accepting that possibility you can more or less attribute anything to aliens, which is not particularly scientific. It'd also be more or less impossible to prove. So even if it is the 'least improbable' explanation I think that just means that the search for better explanations should continue.
